questions.prompt: Which of the following cold email opening lines best follows the four-part structure taught in this lesson?
choices: I hope this email finds you well. I wanted to reach out about our revenue intelligence platform.
As a fellow sales leader, I know how challenging it can be to manage a growing team.
Saw that you posted five SDR job listings last week — when headcount scales that fast, pipeline quality usually becomes the bottleneck.
We work with companies like yours to improve sales productivity. I'd love to share how.
questions.explanation: This option leads with a specific, public trigger (SDR job listings) and immediately connects it to a relevant pain (pipeline quality at scale) — the first two elements of the trigger-relevance-value-CTA structure. The others use filler phrases or generic claims that could apply to any company.

questions.prompt: A rep uses AI to generate a cold email and receives this output: 'I came across your profile and was impressed by your company's growth. I wanted to reach out to introduce our platform, which many companies in your space have found valuable.' What should the rep do?
choices: Send it as-is — AI-generated emails have high deliverability.
Add the prospect's name to the greeting to personalize it, then send.
Delete the draft and start with a specific trigger before re-prompting AI.
Add a case study link to increase credibility, then send.
questions.explanation: The draft contains multiple 'AI-smell' phrases ('I came across your profile,' 'I wanted to reach out,' generic value claim) and zero personalization. The right move is to find a real, specific trigger first, then prompt AI again with that trigger as the foundation.

questions.prompt: A rep wants to A/B test their cold email approach. How does the lesson recommend using AI to produce testable variants efficiently?
choices: Run the same prompt three times and send whichever output looks different.
Ask AI to generate three versions with different lead-ins: one starting with the business trigger, one with the value outcome, one with a direct question.
Ask AI to write the email in three different tones: formal, casual, and humorous.
Generate one strong version and split the send list randomly without varying the email.
questions.explanation: The lesson recommends asking AI for three structurally different versions — leading with the trigger, the value outcome, or a direct question — so you test meaningfully different framings rather than style variations of the same message.
